sections.composition:
### How nodes compose
The pipeline is made of four kinds of step, and any of them may be put anywhere the validator's rules (listed below) allow:
- **agent**: one model call. Its prompt fills each `{{name}}` from a fact (or knob) produced upstream; its reply is written to its first `writes` file and, when it declares `produces`, also becomes that fact. A new agent without `tools` sees only its prompt and the files it names in `sees` (they become its declared reads, pasted in after the prompt): hand it anything else as `{{facts}}`. A file's text becomes a fact through an op that reads the file and `produces` the fact, or when the agent that writes the file declares `produces`.
- **where `{{fact}}` is filled in**: only in an agent's `prompt_template` (its `<id>__task` knob) and its system prompt (its `<id>__system_prompt` knob). Any other knob is read as written, so a `{{fact}}` there would never arrive and is refused (V20).
- **tools**: every existing step keeps its own tool rules, and in this run a new step has no tools.
- **gate**: routes by a verdict, to the out-edge whose `condition` is that verdict. Give each out-edge a single-word condition (`proceed`, `reloop`, `revise` ...). Any declared upstream output can be the verdict: with `"evaluator": "refactory_dsh.snippet:verdict"` the gate reads the verdict from its first `required_reads` file (or, with none, its first `inputs` fact) -- whatever an agent or a code op upstream wrote there: its first word, or else its last line when that is the word alone or the word then `:`, `—`, `–`, `-` or `.` and more (leading markdown or quotes are skipped; a list item or a code fence is not read) -- and the rest of the text is the reason. The word must be one of the conditions (any case) or `halt`, which ends the whole run. Anything else fails that item's run, and so does a first word and a last line that name different verdicts, so tell the writer to start with the word or put it alone on the last line.
- **loop**: a gate's out-edge back to an earlier step. The `loop` operation makes one around a step (step -> gate; gate -> step on `reloop`, gate -> the step's old successor on `proceed`); a reloop hands the gate's reason to the step it goes back to as feedback, and the gate's `max_iterations` bounds how often it may. When a gate would reloop once more than that, its `on_exhausted` decides: `continue` (the default inside the per-item pass) goes on along `proceed` with the last attempt, which is graded as it stands; `fail_item` fails that item only; `halt` ends the whole run (no later item runs). A gate with no forward `proceed` edge defaults to `fail_item`. The last step of the pass can be looped too: the loop then adds a step after the gate to end the pass.
- **running out of output**: a model call that uses its whole output allowance without answering is the model failing that question. It is not retried unless the step opts in (retry.on): the step has no answer, and the item goes on without it (a gate after it sees no answer and may reloop; a fork's join sees that branch without one; a code op's `inp['files']` holds only the files that exist; an item left with nothing to grade scores 0).
- **running out of turns**: an agent that uses its whole turn cap without finishing is the model failing that question, like running out of output. It is not retried unless the step opts in (retry.on): the step has no answer, and the item goes on without it, as above.
- **crashes**: when the worker or product fails (not the model's own output or turn cap), an agent step in the per-item pass that is safe to rerun (no tools, its own report files only, or a workspace) is run again in a fresh session, up to 2 more times; if every session crashes it has no answer, as above. An item that times out is a harness timeout: not caused by the pipeline's design; not a target.
- **fork**: steps run at once between a fork and a join; branches write distinct files and facts. `parallelize` and `branch` wire what the branches make into the step after the join; the written-out `parallel` operation leaves that to you.

One example of each composition shape, with this graph's ids (how to write it; none is preferred):
- a new agent step: {"op": "insert", "before": "implement", "kind": "agent", "text": "<what the new step does>"}
- a parallel fork and join: {"op": "parallelize", "after": "implement", "new": [{"kind": "agent", "text": "<what one branch does>"}, {"kind": "agent", "text": "<what another branch does>"}]}
- a verdict loop (a judge that can send a step back): {"op": "loop", "step": "implement", "judge": "agent", "text": "<what to check>"}
- a route (a judge choosing the next step): {"op": "route", "after": "implement", "judge": "agent", "text": "<how to choose>"}
sections.pipeline_view:
The pipeline, one line per step, generated from the graph in the operators' own words: `sees` lists a step's inputs as `"sees"` names them, `name@maker` (`@run`: no step makes it); a plain op that only assembles a model step's input is folded in as `name (via op: its inputs)`; an agent with tools sees the run dir, its own workspace, or a sealed one (its inputs only); `told` is each knob whose text reaches the step, its opening words (`*` frozen; `?` read by an op with several outputs, for all of them), or a code step's code; `->` what it writes; a per-item block's `item files` are files the task lays into each item's pass, under the same name for every item, and the steps that read them: a new step reads one by naming it (or the data step) in 'sees'; `parallel fork { ... } -> join`; `loop(step, judge ..., max N -> N+1 runs)`; `loop(back_to … step, judge ..., max N -> N+1 runs)`; `route(after step, judge ..., {label: step})`; `fallback(step fails -> step)`; `map(step … step over list, max N)`; `per item (data -> its writes; item files: path seen by step, ...) { ... }`; `step agent on model=M effort=E max_completion_tokens=N`; a loop that does not go on with its last attempt past its cap says so: `past the cap: fail_item` (only that item fails) or `past the cap: halt` (the whole run stops); `[optional]`; `[protected]`.
```text
per item (data -> current_item.json, item/input.xlsx; item files: item/input.xlsx seen by prepare) {
  prepare op  sees current_item.json@data, item/input.xlsx@data  -> input.xlsx, SKILL.md, turn.json, spreadsheet_preview.txt, instruction, spreadsheet_path, output_path, skill_section, has_case
  route(after prepare, judge refactory_packages.spreadsheetbench.ops:has_case, {skip: finalize, proceed: inspect})
    on proceed:
      inspect agent  sees sealed workspace (tools: Bash), instruction@prepare, output_path@prepare, skill_section@prepare, spreadsheet_path@prepare, SKILL.md@prepare, input.xlsx@prepare  told inspect__system_prompt "You are a helpful Spreadsheet Automation Engine…"; inspect__task "<task_context> ## Important - When completing s…"  -> inspect_reply.txt, inspect_notes.md, inspect/.refactory-session.json
      plan agent  sees sealed workspace (tools: Bash), instruction@prepare, output_path@prepare, skill_section@prepare, spreadsheet_path@prepare, SKILL.md@prepare, input.xlsx@prepare, inspect_notes.md@inspect  told plan__system_prompt "You are a helpful Spreadsheet Automation Engine…"; plan__task "<task_context> ## Important - When completing s…"  -> plan_reply.txt, plan.md, plan/.refactory-session.json
      implement agent  sees sealed workspace (tools: Bash), instruction@prepare, output_path@prepare, skill_section@prepare, spreadsheet_path@prepare, SKILL.md@prepare, input.xlsx@prepare, inspect_notes.md@inspect, plan.md@plan  told implement__system_prompt "You are a helpful Spreadsheet Automation Engine…"; implement__task "<task_context> ## Important - When completing s…"  -> implement_reply.txt, output.xlsx, implement/.refactory-session.json
      verify agent  sees sealed workspace (tools: Bash), instruction@prepare, output_path@prepare, skill_section@prepare, spreadsheet_path@prepare, SKILL.md@prepare, input.xlsx@prepare, inspect_notes.md@inspect, output.xlsx@implement,verify, plan.md@plan  told verify__system_prompt "You are a helpful Spreadsheet Automation Engine…"; verify__task "<task_context> ## Important - When completing s…"  -> verify_reply.txt, verify_report.md, output.xlsx, verify/.refactory-session.json
  [protected] finalize op  sees implement/.refactory-session.json@implement, implement_reply.txt@implement, inspect/.refactory-session.json@inspect, inspect_reply.txt@inspect, output.xlsx@implement,verify, plan/.refactory-session.json@plan, plan_reply.txt@plan, turn.json@prepare, verify/.refactory-session.json@verify, verify_reply.txt@verify  -> final.json, conversation.json, pred.xlsx, raw.txt, tool_calls.json, finished
}
```
